title: Chapter 20
content:
A heavy crystal tumbler hurtled across the room, smashing into the wall and shattering into a hundred glittering shards.

Veins bulged along Kim Sun-young’s neck as she shrieked at the top of her lungs. "You brainless, incompetent piece of shit!"

She tore into the young man cowering before her—one of the private fixers her maiden family kept on retainer to handle their dirty laundry.

Sun-young’s father had long been one of Seoul’s most infamous cash-rich loan sharks, a shadow financier of staggering wealth. Years ago, shortly after Sun-young’s marriage, her father had attempted to establish a commercial savings bank, only to hit a brick wall with regulatory licensing from the Financial Supervisory Commission. It was Chairman Kang who had rolled up his sleeves, pulled high-level political strings, and cleared the path for him. Because of that massive debt of gratitude, Sun-young’s family still walked on eggshells around their powerful syndicate son-in-law.

"How could he miss a target sitting right in front of him?!" she hissed, trembling with rage. "You swore he was top-tier! You swore his aim was absolute!"

The fixer swallowed hard, keeping his head bowed low. "The... the mark reacted before the shot landed, ma'am. He must have caught the scope's reflection the split-second the trigger was pulled."

"You useless dog! You dare make excuses to my face?!"

SLAP!

Her hand cracked violently across his cheek.

SLAP! SLAP!

She struck him until his head whipped back and forth, but even that failed to quell her fury. Grabbing decorative objects from the side table, she hurled them at his chest.

Watching from the velvet armchair behind her, Kang Tae-han quietly shook his head over his teacup. To think she manages to hide that vile temper so flawlessly whenever Father is around.

Her foolproof assassination plan had unraveled in a single heartbeat. Tae-han, however, wasn't remotely surprised. There had been several attempts on Kang Il-hyun’s life over the years, and every single time, the bastard had walked away without a scratch.

Chest heaving, Sun-young dropped into the armchair opposite him. Noticing a freshly manicured nail had broken during the assault, she cursed under her breath, pulled a slim cigarette from her designer handbag, and flicked a lighter.

"Surrounded by half-wits who can't execute a single basic task," she spat through a plume of gray smoke.

Tae-han pushed a fresh cup of tea across the table toward her. "I told you to hold off, Mother. If only you had listened to me."

Sun-young’s eyes narrowed into slits. Watching Tae-han immediately wash his hands of the mess made her blood boil. The coward had always been an expert at covering his own skin. How can a grown man have such a pathetic backbone? Then again, that spineless nature is precisely why his younger half-brother is about to steal his birthright right out from under him.

"Don't fret," she muttered coldly. "This wasn't our only window."

"After today's close call, do you really think Il-hyun will sit on his hands?" Tae-han countered. "He’s already scouring every CCTV feed leading into the valley and running thermal drones across the entire mountain range."

Sun-young ground her cigarette out in the crystal tray with brutal force. "Then we just need to find the shooter and silence him before Il-hyun does. We eliminate the evidence before that demon captures him and starts peeling his skin off. I've already dispatched a cleanup team. But if we fail to intercept him first..."

Her voice trailed off, anxiety creeping into her sharp features.

Watching her sweat, a cunning glint sparked behind Tae-han's wire-rimmed glasses. He leaned forward, resting his elbows on his knees.

"I might have a better idea..."

"Speak."

"Why not use Seok-joo?"

Sun-young’s face contorted in instant fury.

"They're the exact same age, and by all accounts, they’ve gotten quite close," Tae-han pressed smoothly. "Using Seok-joo to reel the target in would be far simpler, wouldn't it?"

Sun-young’s cheek twitched, but she remained silent. The entire justification for this reckless scheme was to shield her only son from Il-hyun’s blade; the last thing on earth she wanted was to drag Seok-joo into the crosshairs. If the operation went up in flames, she intended to take the fall alone—she would never allow her boy to be collateral damage.

"Leave Seok-joo out of this."

"Then why drag me into it?" Tae-han sneered softly. "Because I didn't crawl out of your womb?"

"Isn't that obvious?" she shot back without missing a beat. "I have never once considered you, Il-hyun, and Seok-joo to be equals. And don't pretend you ever saw us as family either."

"Ah... Mother. You truly never disappoint."

Tae-han let out a dry, chilling chuckle. Watching her icy resolve, it struck him that despite sharing no blood, Sun-young shared a terrifying amount of DNA with Kang Il-hyun in terms of cruelty.

Ignoring him, she brought her phone to her ear, barking rapid-fire orders to her men: Find the sniper at all costs and bury him deep. The cleanup had officially begun.
Toweling his hair dry after a hot shower, Jakyeong glanced up at the bedroom ceiling.

True to his word, Kang Il-hyun had dispatched technicians to remove the surveillance dome. Jakyeong had swept the entire suite with his bug detector just to be certain, and found zero secondary frequencies. The knowledge that he could finally sleep without an electronic eye glued to his chest felt like lifting a boulder off his lungs.

After finishing with his hair, he turned to the tailored suit laid out on the king-sized bed.

Tonight was the formal family dinner at the Chairman’s main estate, requiring him to dress the part of a high-society heir. Slipping into the crisp dress shirt, the imported silk clung smoothly to his frame. He fastened the buttons and attempted to knot his necktie, but having spent years living in tactical gear and casual tees, his hands felt clumsy.

After three botched attempts, he gave up, settling for a loose, passable knot. Fastening his luxury watch and sliding his horn-rimmed glasses onto the bridge of his nose, he headed downstairs.

In the center of the main hall, Il-hyun was standing with his back turned, finishing a phone call.

The floor-to-ceiling glass panel that had been shattered by high-caliber rounds just hours ago had already been replaced with pristine new ballistic glass. The living room was eerily spotless, radiating an immaculate calm as if the violent assassination attempt had never occurred.

Outside, however, the security perimeter told a different story. Handlers patrolled the lawn with snarling attack dogs, surveillance drones buzzed in grid patterns over the tree line, and the number of armed guards stationed along the stone perimeter walls had doubled.

Ending the call, Il-hyun turned around—and paused.

"Sharp," he murmured, his eyes sweeping over Jakyeong.

Before Jakyeong could process the compliment, Il-hyun closed the distance, reached out, and effortlessly undid Jakyeong's messy tie in a single, fluid pull.

Jakyeong stiffened in surprise, but Il-hyun was already rebuilding the knot from scratch. His long, elegant fingers moved with surgical precision right beneath Jakyeong’s throat. At such close proximity, the rich, woody notes of Il-hyun's aftershave filled his senses.

"Are you feeling up to this?" Il-hyun asked softly.

"Pardon...?"

"You had quite the scare this morning. You could have stayed home and rested. The dinner could easily have been rescheduled."

"No, please... Chairman Kang extended the invitation personally. It would be terribly impolite to decline."

Fastening the tie bar with a crisp click, Il-hyun smoothed the lapels, a look of quiet satisfaction warming his face. His dark eyes traveled slowly from Jakyeong's polished leather shoes all the way up to his face. When their gazes locked, Jakyeong managed an awkward, timid smile.

"Much better."

"Thank you, Director Kang."

Il-hyun extended a formal hand. "Shall we depart, Prince?"

Jakyeong shook his head with a pained, self-deprecating chuckle. He was gradually growing immune to the man's dry, ridiculous teasing.

Il-hyun laughed softly, trading the extended hand for a reassuring pat on Jakyeong's shoulder blade. "Let's move. Seoul traffic will be a nightmare at this hour."

Feeling the heat of that heavy palm against his back, Jakyeong noted the contact, but chose not to pull away.

Just as Il-hyun predicted, the expressway was less of a highway and more of a stationary parking lot. Jakyeong leaned his forehead against the passenger window. City lights danced across the dark ripples of the Han River, shimmering like scattered diamonds. Though he had spent his early childhood in the capital, he had never once set eyes on this glittering side of Seoul before turning ten.

Beside him, Kang Il-hyun stared silently into the night.

The sedan crawled forward in agonizing stop-and-go increments until they finally cleared the bottleneck, slipping into the exclusive hillside enclave where the Chairman resided.

Private security staff were already waiting at the front gates to receive them. Stepping out of the sedan, Jakyeong followed Il-hyun through the heavy mahogany doors.

Chairman Kang’s personal residence was surprisingly modest in scale compared to Il-hyun’s sprawling compound. Apart from a meticulously landscaped traditional garden and a private koi pond, Il-hyun’s fortified estate felt far more suited for an underworld kingpin than this quiet mansion.

Inside the grand foyer, an elderly man in a bespoke butler's suit offered a deep, formal bow.

Il-hyun introduced him as Butler Yang. Though the man's hair was snowy white and his face creased with age, his eyes carried a sharp, piercing lucidity that could rival any seasoned operative.

Following the butler down the hall, Jakyeong discreetly surveyed the interior. His attention was immediately caught by a massive, oil-painted family portrait hanging above the gallery landing. Everyone in the frame was smiling—a picture-perfect, respectable family on the surface.

Butler Yang led them into a grand dining hall centered around a sprawling banquet table. Ornate silver candelabras and lush floral arrangements lined the linen runner, while a fleet of private chefs and servers moved with hushed efficiency. Despite arriving right on time, several family members were already seated.

"Executive Director Kang and Master Jang Yi-an have arrived," Butler Yang announced.

The chatter in the room ceased instantly.

Kang Yu-jung was the first to rise. Just as she had yesterday, she crossed the floor with open arms, wrapping Jakyeong in a warm, welcoming hug while patting his back.

"Welcome! It’s only been a day, but look at you—so good to see you again."

Unlike yesterday's casual attire, she wore an impeccably tailored evening dress, radiating the same intoxicating floral fragrance. Jakyeong—hardly an innocent eighteen-year-old boy—felt an uncharacteristic flutter in his chest. As he flushed with mild embarrassment, his eyes briefly crossed with Il-hyun's.

For reasons unknown, Il-hyun let out a quiet, mocking smirk.

Jakyeong instantly clamped his expression down, wiping away the reaction.

"Pleasure to meet you. I'm Kang Tae-han—Il-hyun's older brother."

A lean man wearing thin wire-rimmed glasses extended a hand. His narrow eyes held the calculating, treacherous gleam of a viper.

"Hello, Director Kang. I'm Jang Yi-an. It's an honor."

"You're the spitting image of your mother," Tae-han remarked with an oily grin. "What a shame. If you'd been born a girl, you would have been quite the beauty."

Beside him, an elegant woman nudged his ribs with a sharp elbow, shooting him a warning glare. Tae-han’s wife.

"I apologize on his behalf," she offered smoothly. "My husband's sense of humor often crosses the line."

One glance was enough to tell she was vastly out of her husband's league in both poise and intellect.

"Not at all, ma'am," Jakyeong replied with practiced deference. "I'll take it as a compliment."

Just then, heavy footsteps echoed from the grand staircase.

"The Chairman and Madam Kim are descending."

The room snapped to attention. Every member of the domestic staff lined the perimeter walls, dropping into deep ninety-degree bows. Look at this royal parade, Jakyeong thought dryly. You'd think the King and Queen of Joseon were making an entrance.

The broad-shouldered patriarch descending the steps was none other than Kang Il-hyun’s father, Chairman Kang Hoon.

Despite his advanced years, the old man radiated an overwhelming, suffocating presence, his eyes burning with the raw, predatory intensity of an apex tiger. Supporting his arm was Kim Sun-young, Seok-joo’s mother.

And trailing sheepishly behind them was Kang Seok-joo himself.

Even riding on the coattails of his terrifying parents, the kid’s eyes were darting around the room, swimming with visible anxiety. The arrogant, swaggering bully who acted like a king in the underground clubs had shrunk into nothing more than a fragile, trembling herbivore inside this house.
